# Incident report: Order lookup 5xx responses (order-tracker)

## 1. Summary

`GET /api/orders/{order_id}` returns HTTP 500 (`ValueError: day is out of range for month`) for express-priority orders placed on one of the last two days of a month. The first failure in the evidence window was at 19:27:47Z, and a burst of three at 19:51:14Z triggered the alert at 19:52Z. Only one order is affected, `express-1002`, and it fails every time it is looked up. Other lookups work: `standard-1001` returned 200 and `standard-1002` returned a 404, which is expected because that order doesn't exist.

## 2. Evidence

**Metrics (Prometheus, 19:25–19:55Z)**
- 7 lookups in total: 4 × `500` with `error.type=ValueError`, 2 × `404`, 1 × `200`.
- 5xx by minute: 19:27 (~1) and 19:51 (~4, which is a rate extrapolation of 3 actual requests). The alert query value was 3.13, above the threshold of 1.

**Logs (Loki)**
- All 4 ERROR records have `order_id=express-1002`, `exception_type=ValueError` and `exception_message="day is out of range for month"`.
- The stack trace ends in application code:
  - `app/main.py:186` `get_order` → `return order_detail(row)`
  - `app/main.py:65` `order_detail` → `placed_at.replace(day=placed_at.day + 2)`
- In the lookup table, every 500 is for `express-1002`. The 200 (`standard-1001`) came one second after the burst, so the service itself is healthy.

**Traces (Tempo)**
- All four traces have `order.id=express-1002` and `url.path=/api/orders/express-1002`: `bff0190f…`, `5845d74c…`, `3f3b09ec…` and `c1fe41ac…`.
- Each has status `STATUS_CODE_ERROR` and an `exception` event with the same ValueError.
- Durations are 6.6–129 ms, so this is not a timeout or a dependency problem. It is an immediate exception.

## 3. Root cause

`app/main.py:65` calculates the estimated delivery date by adding 2 to the day-of-month field:

```python
estimated_at = placed_at.replace(day=placed_at.day + 2)
```

`datetime.replace` doesn't carry over into the next month. When `created_at` falls on a day where `day + 2` is past the end of the month, it raises `ValueError`. That happens on the 30th or 31st of a 31-day month, the 29th or 30th of a 30-day month, and the 27th or 28th of February. The error isn't handled, so FastAPI returns a 500.

**Why only `express-1002`:**
- `order_detail` only runs the date calculation when `priority == "express"` (`app/main.py:63`). Standard orders skip it.
- `express-1002` is seeded with `created_at = previous_month_end` (`app/main.py:45` and `:48`). The last day of any month plus 2 is always out of range, so this order fails on every lookup, whatever the current date is.
- An express order placed mid-month (for example on the 15th) gets a valid result.

**Also affected, but not visible in this alert:**
- `create_order` (`app/main.py:200`) and `update_status` (`app/main.py:214`) both return `get_order(...)`. So these will also return a 500 when the order is express and was placed on one of the last two days of a month:
  - `POST /api/orders` for such an order. The row is committed before the error, so the client sees a 500 even though the order was created.
  - `PATCH` on such an order. The status update is committed before the error in the same way.
- Those routes aren't instrumented (`app/main.py:104-109`), so they don't show up in this alert.
- `GET /api/orders` doesn't call `order_detail`, so it is unaffected.
- The existing tests never look up the express order, which is why this wasn't caught.

## 4. Fix

Use `timedelta`, which rolls over month and year boundaries correctly. `timedelta` is already imported at `app/main.py:5`.

```diff
--- a/app/main.py
+++ b/app/main.py
@@ -62,7 +62,7 @@ def order_detail(row):
     order = as_dict(row)
     if order["priority"] == "express":
         placed_at = datetime.fromisoformat(order["created_at"])
-        estimated_at = placed_at.replace(day=placed_at.day + 2)
+        estimated_at = placed_at + timedelta(days=2)
         order["estimated_delivery"] = estimated_at.date().isoformat()
     return order
```

**Regression test** (add to `tests/test_api.py`):

```python
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("created_at", "expected"),
    [
        ("2026-08-31T12:00:00+00:00", "2026-09-02"),
        ("2026-09-15T12:00:00+00:00", "2026-09-17"),
        ("2026-12-31T12:00:00+00:00", "2027-01-02"),
        ("2027-02-27T12:00:00+00:00", "2027-03-01"),
    ],
)
def test_express_estimated_delivery_crosses_month_end(client, created_at, expected):
    with main.connect() as db:
        db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO orders VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            ("express-edge", "Jo", "Lamp", "express", "received", created_at),
        )
    response = client.get("/api/orders/express-edge")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json()["estimated_delivery"] == expected


def test_seeded_express_order_lookup(client):
    response = client.get("/api/orders/express-1002")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert "estimated_delivery" in response.json()
```

The second test fails today on any date because of how the order is seeded. Before the fix, the four parametrized cases give:
- `2026-08-31` and `2026-12-31`: raise the ValueError.
- `2027-02-27`: also fails, because day 29 doesn't exist in February 2027.
- `2026-09-15`: passes. It is a mid-month control case.

## 5. Mitigation (before the fix ships)

- **Ship the one-line fix as a hotfix.** It is low risk and is the only real remedy. There is no feature flag or config setting that bypasses this code path.
- **Tell the affected customer or client** that the order is fine and only the details view fails. `GET /api/orders` still returns `express-1002`, just without `estimated_delivery`.
- **Silence or acknowledge the alert** with a note linking to this report, so repeat lookups of `express-1002` don't page again. Keep it scoped to this known cause so new failures still alert.
- **Avoid editing `created_at` in the database** to work around the bug. That would corrupt order history. If you do it at all, it needs an explicit decision.
- **Expect more failures near month end.** Today is 2026-09-30, the last day of the month, so every new express order today, and any status update on one, will get a 500 until the fix ships. See the note in section 3.

## 6. Confidence and open questions

**Confidence: high.**
- The stack trace points straight to `app/main.py:65`.
- The error message is exactly what `datetime.replace` raises for an invalid day.
- The seed data at `app/main.py:45-48` explains why this one order fails every time.
- All 4 errors across metrics, logs and traces point to the same order and the same exception.

**Open questions:**
- **Is this a real environment?** Traffic is very low (7 requests), and the Grafana URL is `127.0.0.1`, so this looks like local or dev. I haven't confirmed whether any production-like data has express orders created on the last day or two of a month.
- **Business rule for the delivery estimate.** The fix keeps the current meaning: 2 calendar days in UTC. If "2 days" should mean business days, or should use the customer's timezone, that is a product decision beyond this fix.
- **POST and PATCH failures.** These can't be confirmed from telemetry because those routes aren't instrumented. It may be worth adding instrumentation for them, or alerting on all `/api/orders*` routes.
- **Repeat lookups.** I couldn't tell who or what made the 19:27 lookup and the 19:51 burst of three. It looks like a client retrying or a person refreshing the page.
